researched_by: the council's beach guidance and byelaw pages, individual car park pages, the March 2026 Car Parking Strategy report to Overview and Scrutiny Board, the legacy Borough of Poole consolidation parking order, and BBC/local press on the 2023 PSPO attempt
policy_summary:
Twelve miles of the busiest beach frontage in England, 147 council car parks, and not one designated overnight bay. BCP has zero provision - no aire, no motorhome bays, no waste point, no trial, no proposal. Nothing in the Seafront Strategy, nothing in the March 2026 Car Parking Strategy report, nothing in any consultation found.

What it has instead is a ban on the ACT of sleeping rather than on the vehicle class - and that is the single thing that distinguishes BCP from neighbouring Dorset. Dorset writes 'motorhomes not permitted 10pm to 8am' into its off-street order car park by car park. BCP largely still admits motorhomes (Sandbanks Surface, Queen's Road and Beach Road all list 'motorhome' as an accepted vehicle type) and in places sells them an overnight ticket, while stating flatly in its beach guidance: 'No overnight sleeping or camping is allowed on the beach, seafront, cliffs or car parks', fine up to GBP1,000. The practical result is a legal split a van user has to hold in their head: at Sandbanks and Shore Road you can lawfully park a motorhome from 10pm to 8am for GBP3.50 (free 1 November to 14 March) and you cannot lawfully go to sleep in it.

The legal underpinning is layered rather than single. The legacy Borough of Poole Consolidation Order No. 14 (in force 1 June 2017, covering both on-street and off-street parking places) prohibits using any part of a parking place or any vehicle left in one 'For overnight sleeping or camping purposes'. Bournemouth's general parks and open spaces byelaws forbid camping and, separately, 'no overnight parking, from midnight to 6am'. Christchurch retains a Public Health Act-style byelaw titled 'Tents, Vans, Sheds and similar structures'. Above all of it sit the seafront car park gates: Boscombe Undercliff 8am to midnight behind a 2.1m barrier, Avon Beach 9am to 9pm with gates locked at 10pm, Beach Road 6am to 10pm and closed entirely 1 October to 31 March.

The attempt to replace that patchwork with one clean instrument failed. In January-February 2023 BCP consulted on three PSPOs; the second covered highways and car parks and would have banned overnight sleeping in vehicles outright. In July 2023 Cabinet dropped it - portfolio holder Kieron Wilson said it 'would have been open to legal challenge'. The two survivors (open spaces fire/BBQ, and coastal) took effect 7 November 2023 for three years and are therefore due to lapse or be renewed in November 2026; neither mentions vehicles.

Since then the council has switched weapons from anti-social behaviour law to parking law. The Car Parking Strategy report to Overview and Scrutiny Board on 23 March 2026 (Pincroft, Edwards, Taverner) sets out an Experimental TRO restricting the inland side of Boscombe Overcliff Drive - and, recommended, all roads south of Wentworth Avenue - to 'cars and motorcycles only', on the explicit reasoning that in such bays 'any vehicle designed or adapted for sleeping purposes (campervan or motorhome) can be enforced against' by PCN. A second option is a flat no-parking window, 'for example, no parking between midnight and 5am'. Neither had been made as of late July 2026; the report says recommendations are 'still emerging' pending the seafront paid-parking consultation. The east-side seafront on-street bays remain free overnight today (East Overcliff Drive charges 9am-8pm only), which is precisely why vans gather there.
notes:
The mechanism is the finding. A sleeping ban is legally weaker and evidentially harder than a vehicle-class parking ban, and BCP's own March 2026 report says so: 'unless CEOs can see within vehicles they cannot tell if a vehicle has been adapted. There are also some visitors that use smaller vehicles to sleep in overnight which is also be challenging to enforce against.' That sentence is why the ETRO route - restricting the BAY to cars and motorcycles, so the offence becomes the vehicle's presence rather than what the occupant is doing inside it - is the one being pursued. It is the same manoeuvre North Yorkshire and East Suffolk have made, and it works around exactly the evidential problem that killed the 2023 PSPO.

The same report is unusually candid about displacement: restricting Boscombe Overcliff alone 'would simply shift the problem' into Dingle Road, Montague Road, Portman Crescent and Ravine Road, hence the recommendation to do all roads south of Wentworth Avenue at once. Nobody in this dataset has yet answered the obvious follow-on question - where the displaced vans are supposed to go - because BCP has never offered anywhere.

Enforcement reality is heavy and getting heavier, but it is aimed at daytime illegal parking, not at vans. BCP ran a DfT-approved higher-PCN trial across 543 coastal roads from Sandbanks to Southbourne in August 2025 (GBP160/GBP110, tow release GBP280) and has approval to rerun it 4-31 August 2026. Over 4,000 PCNs were issued on peak weekends. Separately the seafront has 24-hour beach patrols who evict overnight campers, a practice that made national news in 2021 when officers used air horns for hourly wake-up calls. A van parked legally and quietly overnight in a 24-hour car park is not what any of that machinery is looking for; a van with an awning out on Boscombe Overcliff is.

Watch two dates. November 2026: the two 2023 PSPOs reach their three-year expiry and any renewal is the natural moment to retry the vehicle-sleeping clause with better drafting. And the seafront paid-parking extension (consulted June-August 2025, covering Canford Cliffs, Branksome Chine, West Cliff, Boscombe and Southbourne, funding tow trucks) - if charging is extended into the overnight period on those free seafront streets, the free-overnight-on-street position that currently makes BCP tolerable disappears without any van-specific order being made at all.

STEP-2 SWEEP, 27 July 2026 - country parks, council caravan and holiday parks including leased ones, harbours, and sites inherited from Bournemouth, Poole and Christchurch in 2019 were all checked. BCP Council runs NO overnight vehicle or camping provision. The strongest lead was Christchurch: 'Grove Farm Meadow Holiday Caravan Park', Stour Way, BH23 2PQ, now trading as Meadowbank Holidays. It is private and always has been - Meadowbank Holidays Limited, Companies House 01232457, incorporated 5 November 1975, registered office at the park, and Companies House records its former name as GROVE FARM MEADOW HOLIDAY CARAVAN PARK LIMITED. Same private company, rebranded; never a Christchurch Borough Council asset and not inherited by BCP. Upton Country Park, Hengistbury Head, Stanpit Marsh and Kings Park are BCP-owned with no camping or caravanning - the only overnight material the council publishes about Hengistbury Head is enforcement news about unauthorised encampments in the car park. Moors Valley Country Park is NOT a BCP asset: East Dorset DC went into Dorset Council in 2019, and Moors Valley is a Dorset Council / Forestry England joint venture. Poole Harbour Commissioners are an independent statutory trust port established by Act of Parliament in 1895 with its own board, not part of the council, so Poole Quay Boat Haven is not council provision; Mudeford and Christchurch quays are ordinary pay-and-display. Mudeford Sandbank beach huts are council-run overnight accommodation but they are huts, not vehicle pitches, and should not be counted as supply here. Private supply, do not re-research as council: Meadowbank Holidays, Hoburne group (Hoburne Park, Hoburne Naish), Beaulieu Gardens, Woolsbridge Manor Farm, Back of Beyond, Haven and Shorefield parks.
open_questions: Has the Boscombe Overcliff Drive 'cars and motorcycles only' ETRO actually been made? The March 2026 report says it could be delivered 'within weeks' but no notice of making was found by late July 2026.

Is there a current BCP-wide off-street parking places consolidation order, and does it carry the Poole 'overnight sleeping or camping' clause across Bournemouth and Christchurch? Only the legacy Poole Order No. 14 (2017) text could be read; the Traffic Penalty Tribunal repository for BCP stops at 2018.
Were the two November 2023 PSPOs renewed at their three-year expiry in November 2026, and did any renewal reinstate the dropped vehicle-sleeping prohibition?

Text of Christchurch Byelaw 03 'Tents, Vans, Sheds and similar structures' - the PDF could not be retrieved. Whether it bites on a motorhome parked on the highway, or only on sited movable dwellings, is unresolved.

Which of the 147 car parks list 'motorhome' as an accepted vehicle type, and whether any of them has a height barrier that makes the listing academic. Confirmed for Sandbanks Surface, Queen's Road and Beach Road only.
What the seafront paid-parking consultation actually recommended, and whether it extends charging into the overnight period on the currently free seafront streets.
Whether the GBP1,000 figure in the beach guidance is a byelaw level 3 penalty on summary conviction and, if so, under which byelaw - no instrument is cited on the page.

democracy.bcpcouncil.gov.uk is robots-blocked, so the asset register and the appendices to the 2023 Cabinet item 'Transfer of green space assets to Christchurch Town Council' (documents s40234 and s40984) were not read. That is the one place a council-owned-but-leased caravan site would surface.

sites.name: All BCP Council car parks, beaches, seafront and cliffs (no overnight sleeping or camping)
sites.notes: The council-wide rule, and the one that matters most. BCP's beach guidance states: 'No overnight sleeping or camping is allowed on the beach, seafront, cliffs or car parks', with a fine of up to GBP1,000. The readable legal underpinning is the Borough of Poole Consolidation Order No. 14 (sealed 30 May 2017, in force 1 June 2017), which covers on-street and off-street parking places and bars using any part of a parking place or any authorised vehicle left in one 'For overnight sleeping or camping purposes'. Note what this does NOT do: it does not exclude motorhomes as a vehicle class, and several car parks still admit them and sell overnight tickets. The offence is sleeping, not parking - which is precisely the enforcement weakness the council identified in March 2026.

sites.name: Boscombe Overcliff Drive and seafront roads south of Wentworth Avenue (proposed 'cars and motorcycles only' ETRO)
sites.notes: The live threat. Report to Overview and Scrutiny Board, 23 March 2026: 'An ETRO could be utilised to restrict parking on the inland side of it to cars and motorcycles only', extended on recommendation to all roads south of Wentworth Avenue. The stated point is that in such bays 'any vehicle designed or adapted for sleeping purposes (campervan or motorhome) can be enforced against' by PCN, while unconverted vans up to 3500kg stay legal. An alternative option in the same report is 'no parking between midnight and 5am' across the seafront areas. Not made as of late July 2026; the report says recommendations are still emerging. Today these seafront on-street bays are free overnight - East Overcliff Drive is a 24-hour parking place charged only 9am to 8pm - which is why vans congregate there. Linear street restriction, so no single pin.

sites.name: Bournemouth parks, nature reserves and open spaces byelaws
sites.notes: BCP's general byelaws for all Bournemouth parks, nature reserves and open spaces prohibit camping outright and, in the Vehicles section, impose 'no overnight parking, from midnight to 6am'. This catches Hengistbury Head, Kings Park, Turbary Common, Kinson Common and Stour Valley. A midnight-6am parking prohibition on open space land is a cleaner instrument against vans than the sleeping ban, but it applies to green spaces rather than to the seafront car parks where the pressure actually is. No consolidated PDF is published; the wording is taken from the council's byelaws index page.

sites.name: Sandbanks Surface Car Park, Poole
sites.search_hint: Sandbanks surface car park, Banks Road, Poole
sites.notes: The sharpest illustration of BCP's split rule. Open 24 hours, 532 spaces, and 'motorhome' is explicitly listed as an accepted vehicle type alongside car, coach and motorbike. There is a published overnight tariff: GBP3.50 flat, 10pm to 8am, 15 March to 31 October, and free 10pm to 8am from 1 November to 14 March. So a motorhome may lawfully be parked here all night, and cheaply - but sleeping in it is prohibited under the same regime that covers every BCP car park, and the local tourism guide puts it plainly: 'overnight camping and sleeping in your vehicle are strictly prohibited across the entire peninsula.' Not provision: no waste point, no designation, no permission to occupy.
sites.geocode_precision: postcode centroid for the car park address on Banks Road, Sandbanks

sites.name: Shore Road Car Park, Sandbanks
sites.search_hint: Shore Road car park, Sandbanks, Poole
sites.notes: The other Sandbanks beach car park. Same 24-hour opening and same GBP3.50 overnight tariff (10pm-8am summer, free 10pm-8am in winter) as Sandbanks Surface, but the accepted vehicle types are cars and motorbikes only - no motorhome listing. Worth recording alongside its neighbour because the pair show that admission of motorhomes in BCP is a car-park-by-car-park listing decision rather than a policy, and a van user 800m the wrong way along the peninsula is in a different position.
sites.geocode_precision: postcode centroid for the car park postcode given on the council page

sites.name: Queen's Road Car Park, Bournemouth
sites.notes: The one BCP car park the motorhome community actually names. Open 24 hours, charged 24/7, 'motorhome' listed as an accepted vehicle type, and long vehicles are directed to the coach and lorry tariff at GBP11.50 for 24 hours (users report selecting 'truck' in the app). About 10 minutes' walk from the town centre, 20 from the seafront, supermarket adjacent. Parking is legal; sleeping is not, and park4night reviewers say so - 'Great space for LWB campervan... No overnight stays though.' A GBP50 PCN is reported for parking outside a marked bay. Recorded as a restriction rather than provision because nothing here is designated or serviced.
sites.geocode_precision: car park entrance on Queen's Road; park4night pin, corroborated within 60m by the BH2 6BE postcode centroid

sites.name: Boscombe Undercliff Car Park, Bournemouth
sites.search_hint: Boscombe Undercliff car park, Boscombe, Bournemouth
sites.notes: The seafront car park directly below the Boscombe Overcliff pressure point, and physically shut against vans twice over: a 2.1m height barrier, and gates open only 8am to midnight. 355 spaces, cars and motorbikes only, peak tariff to GBP19.10. Van users report the signage as 'you cannot stay overnight and the gates get locked from midnight until 8am', with a release fee reported for vehicles left inside after closing. Subject of parking tariff consultation P136 (8-29 May 2026), which proposed increasing and simplifying the charges - no van-specific change.
sites.geocode_precision: car park on Undercliff Drive below Boscombe cliff; park4night pin, corroborated within 250m by the BH5 1BN postcode centroid

sites.name: Christchurch Byelaw 03 - Tents, Vans, Sheds and similar structures
sites.notes: BCP still publishes a set of inherited Christchurch byelaws, among them 'Byelaw 03: Tents, Vans, Sheds and similar structures' and 'Byelaw 16: Seashores and promenades'. The title of Byelaw 03 is the standard formula for a movable-dwellings control byelaw made under the Public Health Act 1936, which regulates the use of vans and tents for human habitation. The PDF could not be retrieved, so whether it bites on a motorhome parked overnight on a Christchurch street or only on sited encampments is unverified - flagged rather than asserted. Recorded because it is the only instrument in the BCP area that names vans directly.
